newsitem.title: GERMANY: Frankfurt bourse starts down, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Frankfurt bourse starts down, seen consolidating.

text.p: German shares opened thin-volume bourse dealings weaker on Friday after Wall Street closed lower overnight, with dealers saying the market was taking a breather following recent bullish trading.
The DAX index of 30 top blue-chip shares was down 12.64 points, or 0.46 percent, at 2,759.70 by 1032 GMT.
"We're just seeing a small correction," said one dealer. Trade is really quiet. But things have generally been busier in the afternoons this week so the market could pick up."
Newly-floated Deutsche Telekom was the heaviest traded of the DAX stocks, but dealings were much lighter than in previous days.
Shares in the telecommunications giant fell 27 pfennigs to 31.88 marks, with dealers saying they were surprised the stock had fallen to $21 in New York overnight.

Meanwhile, shares in drug group Schering were weaker than the rest of the market, slipping 3.35 marks to 119.45 marks after a U.S. competitor, Biogen Inc, was granted European approval for a multiple sclerosis drug.
But traders said the news had not come as a major surprise and should not pressure the stock for too long.

Shares in metals group Metallgesellschaft, whose place on the DAX index was taken this week by Telekom, was slightly firmer, up 18 pfennigs at 28.38 marks in early bourse dealings, after the firm said pre-tax profit had risen 70 pct for 1995/96.
